claim: Framing: there is no one answer for everyone; owing ₹10,000 and owing ₹10 lakh lead to very different outcomes (on-screen: ₹10,000 vs ₹10 LAKH; RULES · REALITY)

Supported by RBL Bank's Retail Collection Policy (PDF created 19 Jan 2018, opened 2026-10-12) and by the amount-based rules in later rows (late-fee slabs CP-016, PNB commission slabs, DRT only from ₹20 lakh in part 2's rows). No change needed.

claim: The day the payment due date passes, the bank starts counting days past due (on-screen: DAYS PAST DUE)
source_quote: The number of ‘days past due’ and late payment charges shall, however, be computed from the payment due date mentioned in the credit card statement
note: RBI (Commercial Banks – Credit Cards & Debit Cards: Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/155, 28 Nov 2025, para 23(5) (TaxGuru reproduction, opened 2026-10-12). Same sentence in HDFC Bank MITC v4.14 (Oct 2026) section D. Primary RBI circular 12 Nov 2021 (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12194): 'If due date of a loan account is March 31, 2021, and full dues are not received before the lending institution runs the day-end process for this date, the date of overdue shall be March 31, 2021.' Note: the card is reported 'past due' to bureaus and late fees apply only after 3 days past due, but the count itself starts at the due date.

claim: Banks track the account at 30, 60 and 90 days past due, and the system checks it every day (on-screen tag: [RBI | 12 NOV 2021 CIRCULAR])
source_quote: classification of borrower accounts as SMA as well as NPA shall be done as part of day-end process for the relevant date and the SMA or NPA classification date shall be the calendar date for which the day end process is run.
note: Primary RBI page opened 2026-10-12: RBI/2021-2022/125, 'Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning pertaining to Advances - Clarifications', November 12, 2021. Stages in the same circular: 'SMA-0 Upto 30 days', 'SMA-1 More than 30 days and upto 60 days', 'SMA-2 More than 60 days and upto 90 days'; para 5: SMA rules 'are applicable to all loans, including retail loans, irrespective of size of exposure'. Tag name and date are right.

claim: If the minimum due stays unpaid for 90 days after the due date, the bank must classify the card as an NPA, a non-performing asset (on-screen: NPA = BAD LOAN [RBI | IRAC NORMS]; stamp NPA · DAY 91)
source_quote: 4.2.19.2 A credit card account will be treated as non-performing asset if the minimum amount due, as mentioned in the statement, is not paid fully within 90 days from the payment due date mentioned in the statement.
note: RBI Master Circular RBI/2025-26/13 (1 Apr 2025), opened 2026-10-12. Current text, RBI (Commercial Banks – IRACP) Directions 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/164, 28 Nov 2025, para 42(10), same words (TaxGuru copy https://taxguru.in/?p=1005741, opened 2026-10-12). New directions start 1 Apr 2027, so today's rule stands for this film. Day counting (RBI 12 Nov 2021 example): due 31 Mar, NPA at the day-end of 29 Jun, i.e. at the end of day 90 counting the day after the due date as day 1, so the account is an NPA from day 91: the DAY 91 stamp is right. NBFC issuers such as SBI Card follow the same 90-day norm under their own directions (not opened; the VO says 'the bank').

claim: Once the card is an NPA it is a loss for the bank: the bank must set aside about a quarter of what you owe from its own profit (on-screen: ABOUT 25% SET ASIDE [RBI | PROVISIONING RULES])
source_quote: 5.4.2 The ‘unsecured exposures’ which are identified as ‘substandard’ would attract additional provision of 10 per cent, i.e., a total of 25 per cent on the outstanding balance.
note: RBI Master Circular RBI/2025-26/13 (1 Apr 2025), opened 2026-10-12. Current text RBI (Commercial Banks – IRACP) Directions 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/164, 28 Nov 2025), para 85 ('A general provision of 15 per cent on total outstanding shall be made in respect of substandard assets') and para 86 (unsecured substandard: 'a total of 25 per cent on the outstanding balance'), TaxGuru copy https://taxguru.in/?p=1005741. A card is unsecured, and 'substandard' is the first 12 months as NPA. 25% is the regulatory MINIMUM for banks (a bank may provide more); NBFC card issuers such as SBI Card book expected-loss provisions under their own rules (not checked). 'About a quarter' is right; optional wording 'at least a quarter'.

claim: That (the 25% set-aside) is why the calls get louder around this time
source_quote: Concurrent allocation for calling and field. Tele calling team to extend shadow support.
note: The escalation itself is sourced: Bank of Baroda collection RFP (20.08.2022, opened 2026-10-12) adds 'Field Referrals' at 31-60 days and the quoted concurrent calling + field work at 61-90 days; RBL policy: bucket 2 '100% to be referred on field'. The CAUSE ('that is why': the 25% provision) is our inference; no bank or regulator source found (research_rules_A A2.1 also says to call it 'one reason'; this checker's web search 2026-10-12 found none). FIX: 'That is one reason the pressure grows around this time.'

claim: Myth check: some people say interest stops after 90 days; it does not (on-screen: MYTH)
source_quote: If a credit card moves to invalidation/written off status due to non-payment, applicable finance charges will be levied till the receipt of complete payment towards the card outstanding.
note: HDFC Bank KFS cum MITC Version 4.14, October 2026 (updated 9 Oct 2026), opened 2026-10-12. Real case: SBI Card's dues of Rs 1,82,969 pending since November 2017 had become Rs 2,55,662.89 when the account was shown written off (MP State Commission order 28.06.2024, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/68016726/), so the bill kept growing long after day 90. Where the myth comes from: RBI Master Circular RBI/2025-26/13 para 3.1.1 says 'the banks should not charge and take to income account interest on any NPA', which is about the bank's income account (see CP-009). No RBI text stops contractual card interest at 90 days. Practice differs by issuer (some stop sending statements after write-off), so 'it does not stop by any rule' is the most exact form; current wording is acceptable.

claim: The bank cannot count your unpaid interest as income, but your bill can keep growing as per your card terms
source_quote: 3.1.1 The policy of income recognition has to be objective and based on the record of recovery. Therefore, the banks should not charge and take to income account interest on any NPA.
note: RBI Master Circular RBI/2025-26/13 (1 Apr 2025), opened 2026-10-12. Current: IRACP Directions 2025 para 124, 'A bank may recognise income on accrual basis only in respect of credit facilities which are classified as ‘Standard’.' (TaxGuru copy https://taxguru.in/?p=1005741). Bill growth per card terms: HDFC MITC v4.14 finance charges continue till complete payment (CP-008); ICICI Amazon Pay MITC: 'Interest will be charged on the Total Amount Due ... till such time as the previous outstanding amounts are paid in full.'

claim: Banks now update the credit bureaus every fifteen days (on-screen: EVERY 15 DAYS [RBI | FROM 1 JAN 2025])
source_quote: CICs and CIs shall keep the credit information collected/maintained by them updated regularly on a fortnightly basis (i.e., as on 15th and last day of the respective month)
note: RBI/2024-25/60, DoR.FIN.REC.No.32/20.16.056/2024-25, 8 Aug 2024, opened 2026-10-12. Para 4: 'These instructions shall be effective from January 1, 2025.' Tag date is right. 'Your CIBIL' is everyday shorthand; the rule covers all four bureaus (CICs).

claim: The bank must tell you before it reports you to a bureau as a defaulter, and must wait if you have a genuine (pending) dispute (on-screen tag: [RBI | CARD DIRECTIONS 2025, PARA 36])
source_quote: 36. Before reporting default status of a credit cardholder to a Credit Information Company (CIC), the card-issuers shall ensure that they adhere to the procedure, approved by their Board, and intimate the cardholder prior to reporting of the status.
note: RBI (Commercial Banks – Credit Cards & Debit Cards: Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/155, DOR.AUT.REC.No.74/24-01-041/2025-26, 28 Nov 2025 (TaxGuru reproduction, opened 2026-10-12; the RBI copy was not opened). Same para: 'Card-issuers shall be particularly careful in the case of cards where there are pending disputes. The disclosure / release of information, particularly about the default, shall be made only after the dispute is settled.' Para number 36 and year 2025 are right for the commercial-bank version (NBFC issuers such as SBI Card have a parallel direction whose para number was not checked).

claim: In one case a consumer commission held SBI Card at fault (deficient in service) for reporting a customer to CIBIL without proper notice first (on-screen tag: [MP STATE CONSUMER COMMISSION | 2024])
source_quote: On this account we conclude that the District Commission has rightly held the Company deficient in service i.e. by not properly intimating the respondent.
note: SBI Cards & Payments vs Sajji Varghese, M.P. State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bhopal, Appeals 461/2022 and 664/2022, order 28.06.2024, opened 2026-10-12. The State Commission upheld the District Commission's finding, citing RBI guidelines on 'issuing of sufficient notice to such cardholder about the intention to report him/her as defaulter'. Context to keep in mind: the customer was himself a defaulter; relief was a CIBIL correction within 30 days and Rs 2,000 costs. Tag name and year are right.

claim: At SBI Card the card may be blocked from the very first missed payment (on-screen tag: [SBI CARD | FAQ])
source_quote: Irregular payments : First payment default In case you have missed making payment of at least minimum amount due as of latest statement on your SBI Credit Card, your card may be blocked for further usage.
note: SBI Card FAQ 'Credit Card Blocking & Unblocking', opened 2026-10-12. VO correctly says 'may be blocked'. Same page: 'Written-off accounts : More than 6 consecutive payments default'.

claim: A small unpaid bill grows faster than a big one (in percent)
note: OUR CALCULATION (tools/cpm_math.py, re-run 2026-10-12): after 6 months unpaid, ₹10,000 grows 91% and ₹1,00,000 grows 38%. True in percent, not in rupees (₹9,112 vs ₹38,371); C026-C028 make the percent meaning clear. Cause: fixed late-fee slabs (HDFC MITC v4.14, Oct 2026).

claim: Both pay the same interest: 3.75% a month plus 18% GST on it (on-screen: 3.75% A MONTH + 18% GST [HDFC · ICICI · SBI CARD · AXIS | 2026])
source_quote: Overdue interest on extended credit Monthly Rate 3.75% Annual Rate 45% ... Presently the GST rate for banking and financial services is at 18% (applicable on all fees, interest, surcharge and other charges).
note: All four opened 2026-10-12. ICICI Amazon Pay MITC 'Last updated on July10, 2026' (quote above). HDFC MITC v4.14 Oct 2026: 'All other variants 3.75% 45.0%' and 'GST@ 18% of interest and late payment charges'. SBI Card MITC (https://www.sbicard.com/sbi-card-en/assets/docs/pdf/most-important-terms-and-conditions/mitc-english.pdf): 'The current rate of finance charges is upto 3.75% per month [45% per annum]'. Caveats for the description, no script change needed: it is the standard rate (HDFC premium variants such as Infinia are 1.99%; SBI 'upto'); ICICI's MITC adds 'In case of default, interest charges may increase up to a maximum of 3.8% per month (46% per annum).'

claim: Late fee is a fixed amount by slab: ₹750 on a ₹10,000 bill, ₹1,300 on ₹1 lakh (on-screen: LATE FEE BY SLAB [HDFC BANK MITC | SEP 2026]; tags ₹750 and ₹1,300)
source_quote: Charges in case of default (no payment or delayed payment): Basis Credit Card bill amount ... ₹5,001 to ₹10,000 ₹750/- ... More than ₹50,000 ₹1300/-
note: HDFC KFS cum MITC opened 2026-10-12 is now 'Version 4.14 Dated – October 2026' (updated 9 Oct 2026); the writer used v4.13 (Sep 2026). Slabs unchanged. Recommended tag: [HDFC BANK MITC | OCT 2026] or [HDFC BANK MITC | 2026]. Fees exclude GST (header 'Late Payment Charges (Excl. GST)'). ICICI Amazon Pay MITC has the same two slabs.

claim: ₹750 on ₹10,000 is 7.5% every month just as a fee; ₹1,300 on ₹1 lakh is only 1.3% (on-screen: 7.5% vs 1.3% A MONTH)
note: Arithmetic: 750/10,000 = 7.5%; 1,300/1,00,000 = 1.3%. Our arithmetic on HDFC slabs (CP-016). Note: once the unpaid ₹10,000 grows past ₹10,000 the fee moves to the ₹900 slab, so over six months the fee is 7.5%, 7.9%, 7.0%, 6.3%, 5.6%, 5.1% of the running bill (cpm_math). 'Seven and a half percent, every month' is right for a ₹10,000 bill; acceptable as an illustration.

claim: After six months of paying nothing, ₹10,000 becomes about ₹19,000, almost double (on-screen: ₹10,000 → ABOUT ₹19,100 IN 6 MONTHS; stack to ₹19,112)
source_quote: Interest will be charged on the Total Amount Due and on all new transactions except Fees/charges and GST/Taxes (from the transaction date) till such time as the previous outstanding amounts are paid in full.
note: OUR CALCULATION, tools/cpm_math.py re-run 2026-10-12: ₹19,112 (interest ₹2,472, late fees ₹5,250, GST ₹1,390), +91% = almost double. Method checked against its sources: 3.75%/month on principal plus unpaid interest (ICICI quote above; HDFC MITC 'the entire outstanding amount except charges would attract finance charges'); no interest on fees or GST (RBI card directions 2025 para 23(2): 'Card-issuers shall not capitalize i.e., levy interest or any other charges, on the unpaid taxes/levies/charges'); one HDFC late fee per missed due date on the bill amount; GST 18% on interest and fees. Simplified (interest from statement to statement, not from purchase dates). If unpaid interest did not earn interest, the result would be ₹18,850: still 'about nineteen thousand'.

claim: Sunita's ₹1 lakh becomes about ₹1,38,000 (on-screen: ₹1,00,000 → ABOUT ₹1,38,400; stack to ₹1,38,371)
source_quote: If a Cardholder avails of the revolving credit facility of the HDFC Bank Credit Card and hence chooses to pay an amount less than the total amount due reflected in the monthly billing statement, the entire outstanding amount except charges would attract finance charges
note: OUR CALCULATION, tools/cpm_math.py re-run 2026-10-12: ₹1,38,371 (interest ₹24,718, late fees ₹7,800, GST ₹5,853), +38%. Method as CP-018. Sensitivity: without interest on unpaid interest the figure is ₹1,35,754; the tool's compounding matches ICICI's and HDFC's wording, so keep ₹1,38,400, labelled OUR CALCULATION (C030).

claim: For Ravi, two thirds of that jump is only late fees (on-screen: 2/3 OF THE JUMP = LATE FEES)
source_quote: Late Payment Charges (Excl. GST)
note: OUR CALCULATION, tools/cpm_math.py re-run: the 6-month jump is ₹9,112. Late fees alone are ₹5,250 = 58% (about three fifths). Late fees PLUS the 18% GST on them are ₹6,195 = 68% (two thirds); the tool's 'late fees 68%' line multiplies by 1.18. The film defines the late fee as ₹750 without GST (C025), so 'two thirds is only late fees' overstates it. FIX (either): VO 'For Ravi, about two thirds of that jump is late fees and the GST on them.' + on-screen '2/3 OF THE JUMP = LATE FEES + GST'; or VO 'For Ravi, more than half of that jump is only late fees.' + on-screen 'OVER HALF THE JUMP = LATE FEES'. Second sentence ('the smaller your bill, the harder the fees hit') holds: fee share is 68% at ₹10,000 vs 24% at ₹1 lakh (with GST).

claim: This is our own calculation using one bank's (HDFC's) published fees; your bill will differ but the shape is the same (on-screen: OUR CALCULATION · tools/cpm_math.py · NOTHING PAID, NO NEW SPENDS)
source_quote: Charges in case of default (no payment or delayed payment): Basis Credit Card bill amount
note: Label is accurate: the tool uses HDFC's slabs (MITC v4.14, Oct 2026; same slabs as v4.13) and the common 3.75% rate. 'The shape is the same': ICICI Amazon Pay MITC has identical slabs; SBI Card and Axis also charge ₹750 at ₹10,000 and ₹1,300 above ₹50,000 (research_practical §6; not re-opened here, opinion line).

claim: In the first three months it is mostly calls, including automated calls, many from big call centres in cities (on-screen: 1 TO 90 DAYS: CALLS [BANK OF BARODA | COLLECTION TENDER 2022])
source_quote: 1-90 DPD – tele-calling by centralized cell using auto-dialer outbound tele-calling(standardized scripts for different situations)
note: Bank of Baroda 'RFP for Selection of Agency for Collections of Dues', RFP issuance date 20.08.2022 (PDF opened 2026-10-12): tag name and year are right. Same RFP: 'centralized/ regional set up with multi lingual workforce'; tele-calling locations 'South: Hyderabad, Chennai, Bangalore, Mangaluru, Ernakulam'. Caveats: the RFP is for the bank's Retail, MSME and Agri dues (Receivables Management Dept), not BOBCARD credit cards; and it adds 'Field Referrals' from 31-60 days and 'Concurrent allocation for calling and field' at 61-90 days. The VO's 'mostly calls' fits; optional on-screen tweak '1 TO 90 DAYS: MOSTLY CALLS'.

claim: Reminders also come by SMS and WhatsApp
source_quote: Unlike phone calls, emails, SMS, WhatsApp, or other forms of digital communications, field loan collections involve sending field agents directly to the borrower’s location
note: SMS from a card issuer's own terms: HDFC MITC v4.14 (Oct 2026) 'In the event of default, the Cardmember will be sent reminders from time to time ... by post, fax, telephone, e-mail, SMS messaging and/ or engaging third parties to remind, follow up and collect dues.' WhatsApp: two independent collection-tech vendors (Credgenics page above, describing what 'Banks, NBFCs, lending Fintechs, and debt collections agencies' use; Provakil https://provakil.com/legal-collections-management/notice-automation 'Deliver digital notices instantly via SMS, email, and WhatsApp'), both opened 2026-10-12. Secondary (vendor) sources only for WhatsApp, no bank document seen; acceptable for a 'reminders come on WhatsApp too' line.

claim: Banks decide how hard to chase by two things: days late and the money at risk (on-screen tag: [RBL BANK | COLLECTION POLICY])
source_quote: The stage of delinquency and the amount at risk will largely determine the specific collection strategy.
note: RBL Bank 'Collection Policy, Retail Assets' (PDF created 19 Jan 2018), opened 2026-10-12. Tag is right. It is one bank's retail-loan policy ('largely determine'); the VO generalises to 'banks', which the BoB RFP's bucket-wise workflow also supports. Fine as worded.

claim: After that (the early months) many banks hand your account to a recovery agency
source_quote: In the event of default, the Cardmember will be sent reminders from time to time for settlement of any outstanding on the card account, by post, fax, telephone, e-mail, SMS messaging and/ or engaging third parties to remind, follow up and collect dues.
note: HDFC MITC v4.14 (Oct 2026). Also PNB policy (agencies for NPA and written-off accounts) and RBL policy ('field visitations by ... external agency employees'). Timing caveat: outside agencies can come in earlier (BoB's tele-calling vendor works 1-90 DPD; field referrals from 31 DPD), so 'after that' is a simplification; acceptable.

claim: Many agencies earn only a percentage of what they collect; one public sector bank (PNB) pays 7.5% to 15% on accounts up to ₹1 lakh (on-screen: 7.5–15% COMMISSION)
source_quote: The Agency will be paid commission on the amounts recovered as under: ... For A/Cs with O/s upto Rs 1 lac ... Upto 3 years 7.5 % ... Above 3 years upto 5 years 10.0 % ... Beyond 5 years 15.0 %
note: Punjab National Bank, SASTRA Division, Head Office, 'Salient features of policy for engagement of Recovery Agencies/Resolution Agents' (PDF created 14 Jun 2021), opened 2026-10-12. Table is 'For NPA accounts upto Rs 10.00 lacs (suit filed/non-suit filed/decreed & Written Off Accounts)'; the rate rises with the age of the NPA. It covers PNB's NPA loans generally, not cards specifically; the VO does not say cards. Fine.

claim: On-screen source tags for the PNB figures: [PNB | AGENCY TENDER] (C035) and [PNB | TENDER] (C040)
source_quote: SALIENT FEATURES OF POLICY FOR ENGAGEMENT OF RECOVERY AGENCIES/RESOLUTION AGENTS
note: The document is a PNB policy (recovery agencies; a second part is 'SALIENT FEATURES OF POLICY ON ENGAGEMENT OF DETECTIVE AGENCIES'), not a tender. FIX: C035 tag '7.5–15% COMMISSION [PNB | RECOVERY AGENCY POLICY 2021]'; C040 tag '₹7,500 PER PERSON TRACED [PNB | DETECTIVE AGENCY POLICY 2021]'. Year from the PDF's creation date (14 Jun 2021); the text itself is undated, so '2021' can be dropped if preferred.

claim: If you owe ₹10,000, the agency may earn about ₹1,000, and only if you pay in full (on-screen: OUR ESTIMATE)
source_quote: The Agency will be paid commission on the amounts recovered as under:
note: OUR ESTIMATE, labelled on screen. Our arithmetic on PNB's slabs for accounts up to ₹1 lakh: ₹750 (7.5%), ₹1,000 (10%) or ₹1,500 (15%) on a full ₹10,000 recovery; Bank of Maharashtra's 12% slab (research_practical 2.2, not re-opened) gives ₹1,200. 'About a thousand' is the middle of that range. 'Only if you pay in full' means the full thousand; commission is paid on whatever is recovered, so a part payment earns a part. Fine as worded.

claim: Agencies usually work city by city or district by district
source_quote: Recovery Agencies/Resolution Agents shall be empanelled for the entire District or Cluster of Districts.
note: PNB policy (2021), opened 2026-10-12. RBL policy: 'Assignment logic will be done based on strategy considering area, coverage etc.' The OneCard list maps agencies to cities, but also lists several 'All India' agencies (rows 1-3 and 12, e.g. 'FPL Technologies Pvt Ltd All India'), so 'usually' is the right word.

claim: In Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, one card company's (OneCard's) agency list names only Hyderabad, Warangal, Karimnagar, Vizag and Vijayawada (on-screen tag: [ONECARD | AGENCY LIST])
source_quote: 28 CollMan Services Tirupathi Andhra Pradesh NO.19-12-356 BAIRAGIPETTADA ,OPP TO PADMAVATHI PARK ... TIRUPATHI-517501
note: OneCard 'List of Authorized Collection Agencies' (file title Repayment_Agencies_Q3, undated), opened 2026-10-12. claim: For a small amount a long trip to a far village rarely pays for itself, so small dues mostly stay as calls and messages; not a rule, simple business (on-screen: OUR ESTIMATE · NO BANK PUBLISHES A CUT-OFF)
source_quote: 1-90 DPD – tele-calling by centralized cell using auto-dialer outbound tele-calling(standardized scripts for different situations)
note: OUR ESTIMATE, labelled on screen. Inputs: commission on recovery (PNB, CP-026), city/district-mapped agencies (CP-029), tele-calling-led collection (BoB). claim: Finding a person who moved is a paid job: one bank (PNB) pays ₹7,500 for each person traced (on-screen: ₹7,500 PER PERSON TRACED)
source_quote: On receipt of information about whereabouts of the missing/absconding borrower / guarantor / co-borrower / ... Rs. 7,500/- per person subject to maximum fee of Rs. 45,000/-

claim: A ₹7,500 tracing fee is worth it only when the amount owed is big
source_quote: Rs. 7,500/- per person subject to maximum fee of Rs. 45,000/-
note: OUR ESTIMATE (reasoning, not labelled on screen but self-evident: the fee is three quarters of a ₹10,000 due). No source states a threshold. Fine as worded.
